paragraphs: Levi without further designation is Levi bar Sisi.
(a) Yalkut, end of Hosea, §533, at 'Take words with you': good readers, good expounders, such as Levi bar Sisi.

(b) Jerusalem Talmud, end of Mitzvat Ḥalitzah, and Rabbah, Vayishlaḥ, chapter 81: the people of Simonia came to Rabbi and said, 'Give us a man to expound, judge, supervise the synagogue, teach Scripture and Mishnah, and attend to all our needs.' He gave them Levi bar Sisi. They made him a great platform and seated him upon it. They asked: 'With what does a woman with an amputated hand perform ḥalitzah?' He did not answer. 'If she spat blood,' etc.; 'What is the meaning of "I shall tell you what is inscribed in the writing of truth"?' etc. They came to Rabbi, saying, 'Is this how you have fulfilled our request?' He answered, 'By your lives, I gave you a man like myself.' He summoned him and asked about spitting blood; Levi answered, etc., and likewise all the questions. He asked why he had not answered them. Levi said, 'They made me a great platform, and my spirit swelled with pride.' He applied to him, 'If you have acted foolishly in exalting yourself, and if you have devised, put your hand to your mouth,' etc. Rabbah and the Babylonian Talmud have somewhat different wording.

(c) He asked Rabbi [Heilprin’s text reads Rabbah], Shabbat (107b), Zevaḥim (30b). He wrote in his notebook, 'I said before Rabbi'—our holy Rabbi—Shabbat (156a). Rabbi spoke to him, Asarah Yuḥasin (72), and said, 'It seems he has no brain in his head' (see his entry). He performed before Rabbi with eight knives, Sukkah (53a); see Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. He demonstrated kneeling before Rabbi and became lame, the ball of his thigh slipping from its place, Megillah (22, end of side b), Ta'anit (25), and Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 1:5:12 [printed locator: chapter 1, mishnah 8]: Levi bar Sisi became lame and never recovered. The Gemara objects: was his lameness not because he hurled words against Heaven? He decreed a fast, but rain did not come. He said, 'Master of the universe, You have ascended on high and do not have mercy on Your children.' They said both caused it, Sukkah (53a). Berit Shalom, Vayishlaḥ, explains the reason: B.Y. [ב״י; provisionally Beit Yosef] says that one who denies the attributes denies God's providence, saying God's providence is in the upper worlds rather than below. This is as though pressing against the Divine Presence's feet, for 'Heaven is My throne and earth My footstool.' Levi's saying 'You have ascended on high' was thus like pressing against the Divine Presence's feet; therefore the ball of his thigh was pressed out of place, measure for measure. He sent Rabbi beer of thirteen soakings: they poured water over the figs thirteen times, Arvei Pesaḥim (107a); see Arukh, entry magag. An undesignated 'those who learn before the sages' means Levi learning from Rabbi, Sanhedrin (17b); see there. 'They said: Those who learn before Rabbi'—Rashi explains: Levi, Menaḥot (80b); see there at length, and what I wrote under 'those who learn' about differing opinions.

(d) Ketubbot (103): before dying Rabbi instructed that R. Ḥanina bar Ḥama should head the academy. He declined because R. Afes was older by two and a half years. R. Afes became head, while R. Ḥanina bar Ḥama sat outside (outside the study house, not subordinating himself to R. Afes). Rashi, Shabbat (59b), explains that because R. Ḥanina bar Ḥama was distinguished he did not enter R. Afes's study house. Out of respect for R. Ḥanina bar Ḥama, Levi sat beside him: R. Ḥanina bar Ḥama was superior to Levi neither in Torah nor in years, and Levi did not subordinate himself to him. Thus, when R. Afes died and R. Ḥanina bar Ḥama became head, Levi had no one to sit beside and went to Babylonia. This is what they told Rav [Heilprin’s text reads Rabbi]: 'A great man has arrived in Nehardea and expounded that the kelila [head ornament] is permitted.' See R. Yehoshua ben Levi.

(e) Shemuel's colleague; see his entry, where he was Shemuel's teacher. So it appears in HaTekhelet (38b): he told Shemuel, 'Aryokh, remain on your feet until you explain it to me.' See R. Yoshiyah of his generation: it is not proper conduct to speak thus to a superior. Shemuel in Levi's name, Eruvin (10, end of side a). Shemuel's father and Levi prayed in the synagogue of Shaf (see his entry).

(f) Jerusalem Talmud, Ta'anit, chapter 3, halakhah 8: troops came to the city. He took a Torah scroll and ascended the roof, saying, 'Master of the universe, if I have neglected one word of this Torah scroll, let them enter; if not, let them leave.' Immediately they were no longer seen. His student did likewise; his hand withered, and they left. His student's student did likewise: his hand did not wither, and they did not leave, to say that a fool is not harmed. Yalkut, end of Hosea, §533, has some scribal errors.

(g) Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, chapter 2, mishnah 8, and Kohelet Rabbah, at 'The end of the matter': when R. Levi died, Shemuel's father eulogized him, etc.: Levi bar Sisi was as beloved before the Holy One as the whole world (see his entry); a parable, etc. Berakhot (18b): when Shemuel went to the courtyard of death to ask his father where the orphans' money deposited with him was, they told him he had gone to the heavenly academy. Meanwhile he saw Levi sitting outside. He asked why he sat outside—the academy of the other dead—and why he had not gone up. Levi said, 'They told me: for all the years you did not go up to R. Afes's academy and hurt his feelings, we shall not admit you to the heavenly academy,' etc. Shemuel told his father, 'If I am esteemed, let them admit Levi'; they admitted him (see his entry). They sent to ask Levi, 'What is the law of a bed canopy?' By the time the messenger went, Levi had died (see Rav Menashya of Medvil). R. Shemaya son of R. Zeira recited in the Kiddushin of Levi's school (see his entry). At the end of Sotah, Levi says: even those of reeds and of ḥilat [plant term unresolved] are forbidden. Arukh and Maimonides ruled like Levi because he was greater than Rav and Shemuel (Be'er Sheva).

(h) R. Abba bar Kahana heard him expound and kissed his head, Midrash Kohelet, at 'A man to whom God gives.' In R. Abba's name; see R. Mani son of R. Yonah. R. Abba bar Pappi, in his name. R. Abba bar Safra, in his name. R. Avdimi of Ḥaifa, in his name. Avlet asked Levi, Jerusalem Talmud, Kirah, halakhah 3. R. Aḥa, in his name. R. Aḥa bar Shikla. In R. Aḥa bar Ḥanina's name; in R. Aḥa bar Shila of Kefar Tamarta's name. R. Afes (see above). R. Berekhya, in his name. When Rav Dimi came, he said: R. Luai recited, etc.; a contradiction between a teaching of Luai's school and what Levi recited, Zevaḥim (115a). R. Zavda, in his name. Zavdi ben Levi may be his son. R. Zekharyah, his son-in-law, speaks in his name. R. Ḥiyya bar Pappi, in his name. R. Ḥakhinai, in his name. In R. Ḥama bar Ukva's name. In R. Ḥama bar Ḥanina's name. R. Ḥanina bar Ḥama (see above). R. Ḥanina Shalka. R. Yehudah, his son. R. Yehudah bar Simon, in his name. R. Yehudah ben Beteira [ריב״ב], in his time; see his entry. This requires examination. R. Yehudah bar Neron. R. Yehoshua of Sikhnin, in his name. In R. Yoḥanan ben Shaul's name; in R. Yoḥanan ben Sha'una's name. R. Yose son of R. Bun. In R. Yose bar Ilai's name. Yosef Rishba. R. Yaakov bar Avina, in his name. R. Kohen, in his name. In R. Meir's name, Sukkah (8b). R. Mana of Sha'av, in his name. R. Mani son of R. Yonah, in his name. In R. Menaḥem of Galya's name. In R. Menasya's name. R. Levi, in R. Nezira's name, Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 12, and likewise end of chapter 82; that account in chapter 11 has Ze'eira. R. Menashya of Medvil, in his time. R. Mattana, in his name. R. Simon ben Kozot, in his name. Mar Ukva, in his name. R. Pinḥas, in his name. He said, 'Rav Pappi said.' He disagrees with Rav, HaMafkid (41a). Rabbi (see above). In R. Shila of Kefar Tamarta's name. Shemuel, his colleague or student (see above).
